obstacle-detection.title: Obstacle avoidance: Controlling loop execution
body: Scout drone Sigma is flying a low-altitude survey corridor inside the Mawrth Vallis gorge. Under nominal conditions, a counter loop `for` visits sectors 1 through 10 in automated succession.

However, real planetary terrain is unpredictable. A sudden canyon rockfall can obstruct the flight path, an unexpected dust vortex can blind optical navigation, or an overheating thruster can demand immediate landing.
When an emergency occurs, the drone cannot blindly continue to sectors 5, 6, and 7 waiting for the loop counter to expire. It must possess the ability to abort the remaining loop entirely.

Conversely, if one specific sector is merely shadowed by a cliff, the drone might skip scanning that single sector and immediately proceed to the next. In C++, these two real-time interventions are handled by `break` and `continue`.

archive.title: Reactive obstacle avoidance in autonomous planetary rovers
body: On the Mars Curiosity and Perseverance rovers, autonomous driving software (AutoNav) runs a high-rate stereo-vision obstacle detection loop.

While evaluating potential driving arcs, the algorithm loops across prospective path vectors. If point-cloud disparity algorithms detect a hazardous boulder or drop-off on an arc, the computer does not waste processing time analyzing the rest of that dangerous path.

It uses early loop termination (`break`) to abandon the blocked arc immediately and evaluate the next corridor. Such early-exit patterns are essential in embedded aerospace systems where real-time CPU cycles are constrained.
sources: NASA JPL, 'Autonomous Hazard Detection and Avoidance on Mars 2020'
Mark Maimone et al., 'Autonomous Navigation for Mars Exploration Rovers'

break-in-loops.title: The break statement in loops
compareCaptions: Clean early exit: break immediately halts the loop upon meeting the trigger condition
Clumsy flag logic: auxiliary boolean variable clutters condition and requires extra checks
body: You already encountered `break` in Chapter 11 inside `switch` statements to prevent fall-through. When placed inside a loop (`for`, `while`, or `do-while`), `break` performs an even more dramatic action:
**It immediately terminates the loop entirely!**
Execution instantly leaps past the loop's closing brace `}`, continuing with the very next statement in the program.
> **Innermost loop rule:** If loops are nested within one another, `break` only exits the **innermost** loop in which it resides. Outer enclosing loops will continue running.

predict-break-output.title: Tracing early termination
predict-break-output.task: What output will this program produce? Trace the counter values until the break triggers.
predict-break-output.hint: The loop counts from i = 1 to 6. When i reaches 4, the if condition triggers break. Does 4 get printed?
predict-break-output.explain: For `i = 1`, `2`, and `3`, the condition `i == 4` is false, so `123` is printed. When `i` becomes 4, the `if` condition succeeds and executes `break;`. The loop terminates immediately without printing 4, and the trailing exclamation mark `!` is output, producing `123!`.

canyon-obstacle-abort.title: Canyon obstacle abort controller
canyon-obstacle-abort.task:
Program Scout drone Sigma's patrol route with an early obstacle abort (test input: `3`):
1. Read the blocked sector number `int obstacle` from `cin`.
2. In a `for` loop for `int sector = 1` up to and including `5` (`sector <= 5`): if `sector == obstacle`, print `OBSTACLE AT SECTOR ` followed by `sector`, a newline, and immediately exit the loop with `break;`; otherwise (`else`), print `SECTOR ` followed by `sector`, ` CLEARED`, and a newline.
3. After the loop ends (outside the braces), print `PATROL ENDED` and a newline.
canyon-obstacle-abort.hint: Use `if (sector == obstacle) { cout << "OBSTACLE AT SECTOR " << sector << endl; break; } else { ... }`.
canyon-obstacle-abort.solutionNote: With obstacle at 3, sectors 1 and 2 clear successfully, sector 3 prints the obstacle alert, and break terminates the loop.

continue-skip-iteration.title: The continue statement: Jump to next cycle
compareCaptions: Clean guard clause: continue skips the remainder of iteration cleanly at the top
Inverted if nesting: wrapping the entire body inside an if statement creates unnecessary indentation
body: While `break` completely abandons the entire loop, `continue` is much gentler:
**It skips only the remainder of the CURRENT iteration!**
When `continue` is reached, execution jumps immediately to the end of the loop body for that single pass:
- In a `for` loop: execution jumps straight to the **update expression** (`i++`), tests the condition, and proceeds with the next iteration.
- In a `while` loop: execution jumps straight to the **condition check**.

!> **The while-continue trap.** If you call `continue` in a `while` loop before incrementing your counter variable, the counter is never updated, creating an infinite loop! Always ensure the counter variable is updated before `continue` runs.

predict-continue-output.title: Predicting filtered iteration output
predict-continue-output.task: What output will this program produce? Trace which numbers are skipped by continue.
predict-continue-output.hint: The expression i % 2 == 0 checks whether i is an even number. If even, continue skips the cout statement.
predict-continue-output.explain: When `i` is 2 or 4, `i % 2 == 0` evaluates to true, triggering `continue;` and skipping the `cout` statement. Only odd numbers (1, 3, 5) reach the output line, producing `135`.

shadow-sector-bypass.title: Shadow sector bypass filter
shadow-sector-bypass.task:
Program Sigma's LiDAR scanner to skip shadowed sectors using `continue` (test input: `2`):
1. Read shadowed sector number `int shadow` from `cin`.
2. In a `for` loop for `int sector = 1` up to and including `5` (`sector <= 5`):
3. If `sector == shadow`, print `SKIPPING SHADOW SECTOR ` followed by `sector`, a newline, and skip to the next iteration with `continue;`.
4. Print `SCANNING SECTOR ` followed by `sector` and a newline.
5. After the loop completes, print `SCAN COMPLETE` and a newline.
shadow-sector-bypass.hint: Write `if (sector == shadow) { cout << "SKIPPING SHADOW SECTOR " << sector << endl; continue; }` followed by the regular scanning print.
shadow-sector-bypass.solutionNote: With shadow sector 2, sector 2 triggers the bypass and skips scanning, while sectors 1, 3, 4, and 5 are scanned.

find-continue-while-trap.title: The while-continue infinite loop trap
find-continue-while-trap.task: Click on the line causing this program to lock up in an infinite loop.
find-continue-while-trap.hint: Look at line 8: when sector is 3, what does continue do? Does sector++ ever execute?
find-continue-while-trap.explain: On line 8, `continue;` jumps immediately back to `while (sector <= 5)`. Because `sector++` on line 11 is skipped, `sector` remains 3 forever! The condition `3 <= 5` stays permanently true, freezing the program in an infinite loop.

predict-break-vs-continue.title: Predicting combined break and continue
predict-break-vs-continue.task: What sequence of digits will this program output? Trace both break and continue conditions.
predict-break-vs-continue.hint: When i == 2, continue skips printing. When i == 5, break terminates the loop completely.
predict-break-vs-continue.explain: For `i = 1`, prints 1. For `i = 2`, `continue` skips printing. For `i = 3`, prints 3. For `i = 4`, prints 4. For `i = 5`, `break` halts the loop before printing 5 or 6. The output is `134`.

search-target-beacon.title: Bonus challenge: Emergency beacon frequency scanner
search-target-beacon.task:
Search frequency channels until an emergency beacon signal is detected (test input: `102`):
1. Read the target beacon frequency `int target` from `cin`.
2. In a `for` loop from `int freq = 100` up to and including `104` (`freq <= 104`):
3. If `freq == target`, print `BEACON FOUND AT ` followed by `freq`, a newline, and terminate search with `break;`.
4. Otherwise (`else`), print `SEARCHING ` followed by `freq` and a newline.
5. After the loop completes, print `SEARCH SEQUENCE FINISHED` and a newline.
search-target-beacon.hint: Use `if (freq == target) { cout << "BEACON FOUND AT " << freq << endl; break; } else { cout << "SEARCHING " << freq << endl; }`.
search-target-beacon.solutionNote: With target 102, frequencies 100 and 101 are searched, 102 triggers the match, and break concludes the search.

recap.title: Mission 15 summary: Loop control mastered
body: Congratulations! You now possess full control over loops in C++. Drones Sigma and Delta can dynamically abort hazardous routes with `break` and skip unviable data sectors with `continue`.

| Statement | Effect on current loop | What executes next | Common beginner trap |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `break;` | Immediately terminates the loop | First statement after loop closing brace `}` | Confusing with `break` in `switch` |
| `continue;` | Skips remainder of current iteration | Loop update (`for`) or condition test (`while`) | Skipping counter increment in `while` -> freeze |

Next, in Chapter 16, awaits Block 2's grand finale: **PRAKTIKUMS: skenēšanas cikls**! We will synthesize every looping construct (`while`, `do-while`, `for`, `break`, `continue`) into a complete autonomous sector mapping mission.
